analysis.title: The AI trade is breaking apart
key_insights: SOX continues to fall further below its 200-day moving average, and the note sees little evidence of stabilization.
Goldman's trading desk sees a rotation within tech: hyperscalers outperformed by 350bps while semiconductors lagged by 250bps, as investors use semis as a source of funds.

Goldman's desk reasoning: restrictions on data center expansion could make existing compute capacity more valuable, supporting pricing power, reducing capex needs and potentially freeing cash for buybacks.
The broader AI complex is under pressure: AI Leaders down 500bps, power-related stocks down 600bps, data centers down 540bps.
The note suggests the next phase of the AI trade may favour those monetizing compute rather than those building it.
Goldman's Callahan notes semiconductor forward P/E fell more than 40% over two months, from 28x to 16x.
SOX trades at roughly a 2-turn forward P/E discount to the S&P 500, near the widest gap in 15 years.
Semiconductor volatility (VXSMH) has barely moved while the VIX is collapsing, which the note reads as a sign that semiconductor stress is not over.

Outperformed semis by 350bps as existing compute capacity may gain pricing power and capex needs may fall.

Continued technical damage in SOX below its 200-day moving average.
vol_and_positioning: VIX is collapsing while semiconductor volatility (VXSMH) has barely budged, leaving a large gap between the two.
The note says the broader market may be stabilizing but semiconductor volatility suggests stress is far from over.
SOX trades at roughly a 2-turn forward P/E discount to the S&P 500, near the widest gap in 15 years.
